tuas: tuus, -a, -um — your, yours (sg. poss.) (f. acc. pl.)
tulisset: ferō, ferre, tulī, lātum — to carry, bring, bear (3rd sg. plupf. subj.)
turbatus: turbō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to disturb, throw into confusion; turbātus (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg.)
ulixes: Ulixēs, -is (m.) — Ulysses, king of Ithaca (nom. sg.)
ulixi: Ulixēs, -is (m.) — Ulysses, king of Ithaca (gen. sg. Ulixī; also dat. sg.)
ultro: ultrō (adv.) — of one's own accord, voluntarily; besides
umida: ūmidus, -a, -um — damp, moist, dewy (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
undique: undique (adv.) — from all sides, on every side
urere: ūrō, -ere, ussī, ustum — to burn, set on fire (pres. inf.)
utrumque: uterque, utraque, utrumque — each of two, both (n. acc. sg.: in utrumque, for either event)
vagatur: vagor, -ārī, -ātus sum — to wander, roam, spread abroad (3rd sg. pres., deponent)
validis: validus, -a, -um — strong, powerful, stout (m./n. abl./dat. pl.)
vanum: vānus, -a, -um — empty, false, untrustworthy (m. acc. sg.; n. nom./acc. sg.)
velit: volō, velle, voluī — to wish, want, be willing (3rd sg. pres. subj.)
venientibus: veniō, -īre, vēnī, ventum — to come; veniēns (pres. part., m./f./n. dat./abl. pl.)
venturaque: veniō, -īre, vēnī, ventum — to come; ventūrus (fut. part., f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.) + -que 'and'
versare: versō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to turn over, turn about, ply, contrive (pres. inf.)
vetabat: vetō, -āre, vetuī, vetitum — to forbid, prohibit (3rd sg. impf.)
videre: videō, -ēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, behold (pres. inf.)
vidi: videō, -ēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, behold (1st sg. perf.)
vigebat: vigeō, -ēre, viguī — to be vigorous, flourish, be strong (3rd sg. impf.)
viribus: vīs, vīs (f.) — force, strength; pl. vīrēs, vīrium, strength (abl./dat. pl.)
visendi: videō, -ēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see; vīsendī (gerund/gerundive), of seeing (gen. sg.)
volgum: vulgus (volgus), -ī (n.) — common people, crowd, mob (acc. sg.; older spelling)
